fieldMarks: Medium to large cottontail, 35-39 cm, 0.7-1.2 kg, with long hind legs.
Greyish-brown upperparts, white belly; tail large, dark above and light below.
Hind legs covered with long, dense reddish-brown hair.
Short, rounded ears with black tips and long hairs on the inner surfaces.
behavior: Solitary and crepuscular, feeding in or near sheltering brush; active year-round.
When frightened, runs a few metres to cover and freezes with ears erect before hopping away.
Prefers grasses; when grass is scarce eats sagebrush and western juniper.
habitat: Brushy or wooded slopes and riverbanks with grasses, willows and especially sagebrush; on sparse rocky slopes it hides in burrows or rock crevices.
range: Mostly the western United States from the Sierra Nevada east to Montana's eastern border and south to central New Mexico and Arizona, reaching into a small area of southern Canada north of Montana and Washington.
